historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists

starting.description: Greater weight and fat reduction from co-administered GIP and GLP-1 analogues in obese mice supplied Finan's team with an experimental reason to pursue a single dual agonist. The LY3298176 investigators cited this prior combination result among the biological reasons for pursuing GIP addition to GLP-1 activity.

inspiration.description: The observed combined actions of GIP and GLP-1 analogues, along with incretin physiology and the hormone-derived peptide sequences, informed the engineering. The LY3298176 authors specifically cite the Finan combination findings and call their peptide GIP-based; a later investigator account describes adding GLP-1 activity to a GIP sequence.

steps.description: Combining selective incretin analogues enhanced weight-lowering in diet-induced obese mice relative to either alone at the tested doses, leading the investigators to pursue a single co-agonist.
Investigators built and tested a sequence-modified peptide with GIP and GLP-1 activity from a previously studied dual GLP-1/glucagon peptide, then modified candidates to extend exposure.

Citing prior dual incretin studies including the co-administration experiment, Lilly investigators developed a GIP-based, fatty-acid-modified dual agonist, LY3298176, and tested both receptor activities in cells and mice. They later identified LY3298176 as tirzepatide and described engineering GLP-1 activity into the GIP sequence.
The LY3298176 investigators reported a phase 1 clinical program and a four-week proof-of-concept trial in type 2 diabetes.

design.description: The Finan team engineered balanced receptor co-agonism and selectivity by sequence changes and lengthened exposure by lipidation or PEGylation. LY3298176, or tirzepatide, is a different GIP-based engineered peptide, with GLP-1 activity introduced into the GIP sequence, stronger GIPR than GLP-1R potency in the reported in-vitro assays and a fatty-acid linker to enable prolonged exposure.

circumstances.description: The comparison of co-administered analogues and subsequent single-peptide engineering were planned experiments in the Finan program; the Lilly team designed LY3298176 to test dual incretin activity.

limits: Finan's balanced hybrid and Lilly's GIP-based LY3298176 are related class-development contributions with distinct reported architectures; the retrieved accounts do not by themselves demonstrate direct chemical descent.
conflicts: Finan 2013 describes enhanced first-phase insulin secretion during human GIP/GLP-1 co-infusion and cites Mentis 2011 as reference 19. Mentis instead reports no additional overall insulinotropic or glucose-lowering effect in its six-hour type 2 diabetes experiment, and no first-phase analysis was found in that article. This citation discrepancy is not resolved by extrapolating either study; it does not negate Finan's separately reported mouse weight observation.
gaps: The origin of Finan et al.'s first-phase co-infusion claim is not established by the cited Mentis study as read.
The available reports do not establish the complete chronology of internal Lilly design decisions or direct chemical descent from Finan's hybrid.
